title: Mesh Backhaul Quality Warning
dataSources: UniFi controller events (`unifi:event`), Pi-hole query log (`pihole:query`), AdGuard Home (`adguard:query`), speedtest-cli results (`speedtest:result`), router/firewall syslog, ISP uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: UniFi / router syslog, Pi-hole/AdGuard, and scheduled speedtests via HEC scripted inputs and the Universal Forwarder.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=unifi:event
| stats avg(backhaul_signal_dbm) as avg_signal, min(backhaul_signal_dbm) as worst_signal by ap_name
| where avg_signal<-70 OR worst_signal<-80
| sort avg_signal
description: Monitors the health of mesh or wireless uplinks so you know when an AP is still online but leaning on a weak backhaul link.
value: Backhaul quality is a hidden dependency for mesh systems; poor uplinks explain a lot of room-specific slowness that client metrics alone miss.
implementation: Forward backhaul signal telemetry from the controller; alert when an AP's uplink quality drops below your comfort threshold.
visualization: Table of APs by average and worst backhaul signal.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces when a Wi-Fi access point is still online but talking to the rest of the network over a weak link.
